# Writing .learningmap Files

> A `.learningmap` file is a JSON document (version 1) describing a visual learning
> path: nodes (topics, tasks, images, text) connected by edges, plus map settings.
> It is the file format used by Learningmap (https://learningmap.app), edited in the
> web app or the VS Code extension "Learningmap Studio", and rendered by the
> `@openpatch/learningmap` React component and web component.

## File Structure

A `.learningmap` file is a single JSON object with these top-level keys:

- `nodes` (array, required): all nodes on the canvas.
- `edges` (array, required): connections between nodes.
- `settings` (object, required): map-level configuration.
- `version` (number, required): currently always `1`.
- `type` (string, optional): set to `"learningmap"`.
- `source` (string, optional): e.g. `"https://learningmap.app"`.

Coordinates (`position.x`, `position.y`) are canvas pixel values; any numbers are valid.

## Nodes

Each node has:

- `id` (string, required, must be unique): any string, e.g. `"1"` or `"node-1762086584942"`.
- `type` (string, required): one of `"topic"`, `"task"`, `"image"`, `"text"`.
- `position` (object, required): `{ "x": number, "y": number }`.
- `zIndex` (number, optional): topics/tasks typically `30`, background image/text nodes `10`–`20`.
- `width` / `height` (number, optional): used by image nodes.
- `data` (object, required): see below.

### Node types

- `topic`: a section/grouping node. Completed automatically when its `completion.needs`
  nodes are all completed; shows `mastered` when `completion.optional` nodes are also done.
- `task`: an actionable activity the learner marks as started/completed.
- `image`: background decoration; `data.data` holds a base64 data-URI image, `data.caption`
  supports markdown links.
- `text`: background text/emoji; `data.text` is the content, optional `data.fontSize`,
  `data.color`, `data.rotation`.

### Node `data` fields (topic/task)

- `state` (string, required): one of `"locked"`, `"unlocked"`, `"started"`, `"completed"`, `"mastered"`.
  This is the learner's progress state; in authored files use `"locked"` or `"unlocked"`.
- `label` (string, required): short title shown on the node.
- `description` (string, optional): long markdown text (headings, lists, links supported).
- `duration` (string, optional): e.g. `"5 min"`.
- `summary` (string, optional): short badge text, e.g. `"Optional"`.
- `color` (string, optional): a color name such as `"yellow"`, `"red"`, `"lila"`, used for visual grouping.
- `fontSize` (number, optional): label font size.
- `locked` (boolean, optional): prevents dragging/selecting the node in the editor.
- `video` (string, optional): URL of an embedded video.
- `unlock` (object, optional): conditions to unlock the node:
  - `after` (array of node ids): node unlocks when ALL listed nodes are completed/mastered.
  - `date` (string): ISO date after which the node unlocks.
  - `password` (string): password required to unlock.
- `completion` (object, optional, mainly for topics):
  - `needs` (array of node ids): required for the topic to be `completed`.
  - `optional` (array of node ids): completing these too upgrades the topic to `mastered`.
- `resources` (array, optional): `{ "label": string, "url"?: string, "type"?: "url" | "book", "bookName"?: string, "bookLocation"?: string }`.

Note: edges are purely visual. Unlock/completion logic is driven ONLY by
`unlock.after` and `completion.needs`/`optional`, not by edges.

## Edges

Each edge has:

- `id` (string, required): convention `"e<source>-<target>"` or React Flow style
  `"xy-edge__<source><sourceHandle>-<target><targetHandle>"`.
- `source` (string, required): id of the source node.
- `target` (string, required): id of the target node.
- `sourceHandle` / `targetHandle` (string, optional): `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, `"right"`.
- `type` (string, optional): e.g. `"default"`.
- `animated` (boolean, optional).
- `style` (object, optional): `{ "stroke": "#hexcolor", "strokeWidth": number }`.

## Settings

`settings` may contain:

- `title` (string): map title.
- `id` (string): map identifier.
- `language` (string): e.g. `"en"`.
- `background` (object): `{ "color": "#hexcolor", "nodes": [...] }` for background decorations.
- `viewport` (object): `{ "x": number, "y": number, "zoom": number }` initial camera.
- `defaultEdgeType` (string) and `defaultEdgeColor` (string): defaults for new edges.

## Minimal Example

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "1",
      "type": "topic",
      "position": { "x": 192, "y": 271 },
      "zIndex": 30,
      "data": {
        "state": "unlocked",
        "label": "Getting Started",
        "description": "Learn the basics.",
        "completion": { "needs": ["2"], "optional": [] }
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "2",
      "type": "task",
      "position": { "x": 192, "y": 80 },
      "zIndex": 30,
      "data": {
        "state": "unlocked",
        "label": "Read the intro",
        "unlock": { "after": [] }
      }
    }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "id": "e2-1", "source": "2", "target": "1" }
  ],
  "settings": {
    "title": "My First Learningmap",
    "background": { "color": "#ffffff" }
  },
  "version": 1,
  "type": "learningmap",
  "source": "https://learningmap.app"
}
```

## Best Practices

- Always include `"version": 1` and `"type": "learningmap"`.
- Use stable, unique node ids; reference them exactly in `unlock.after` and `completion`.
- Give at least one node `state: "unlocked"` (typically the entry topic/task) so learners can start.
- Use `description` with markdown for rich instructions; keep `label` short and action-oriented.
- Prefer `topic` nodes with `completion.needs` to structure progress; use `unlock.after` on
  tasks to gate prerequisites. Remember edges do not affect logic.
- Keep image nodes (`type: "image"`) at lower `zIndex` so they stay in the background.
